notes:
I don't have any notes for you on Job 38:1-20 yet. My first attempt to read the commentary pages broke because of a mistake in my own code, and the tool then cut me off before I could retry. Because of that, I didn't read any page from the approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written notes from memory, and I can't give you any page URLs as sources.

When you ask again, I'll start with these pages:
- **Verse-by-verse (traditional reading):** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/job-38/, plus the Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary and Gill pages for Job 38 on biblehub.com, and the preceptaustin.org Job 38 commentary.
- **Differences between Protestant traditions:** Wesley's Notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon sermons (spurgeon.org), and Ligonier or Desiring God pieces on the whirlwind speeches and on God's answer to suffering.
- **Other views:** the netbible.org notes on Job 38, and bibleodyssey.org articles on Job and creation. I'd also check the "sons of God" and "morning stars" lines (v. 7) on gotquestions.org and catholic.com, and look for Church Fathers' readings of Job on newadvent.org.
